metas.name: Buddy's Beer Garden
metas.description: Buddy's musical antics as a waiter at a German beer garden are truly delightful! Cookie appears as a cigarette girl and scarf-dancer, and a drag-decked lounge-singing Buddy brings down the house.

metas.name: Buddy the Gob
metas.description: Buddy is a US sailor on shore leave in China, where he rescues a girl who is about to be sacrificed to a dragon.

metas.name: Buddy and Towser
metas.description: On a winter night, Buddy charges Towser with the task of guarding his prize chickens, and then goes to bed. A fox enters the henhouse and is driven out by the hens and some ducks by having eggs thrown at him.

metas.name: Beauty and the Beast
metas.description: A little girl is eating too many snacks when she doesn't realize that it is her bedtime. Then the Sandman comes out of nowhere and, sure enough, the girl falls asleep in the blink of an eye. Just then, she has a dream that she is in Toyland, where she encounters all kinds of fairy tale characters.

metas.name: Buddy's Trolley Troubles
metas.description: Buddy runs his own trolley. Most of it seems to be a musical number. However, there is a criminal living in the ditches as he breaks loose and hijacks Buddy's trolley.

metas.name: Goin' to Heaven on a Mule
metas.description: A lazy farm hand must choose between "good" and "evil" regarding alcohol. His nightmare shows him going to heaven on a mule, but when he's there he gets into the jug of booze again and gets kicked to Hades.

metas.name: How Do I Know It's Sunday
metas.description: Inside a general store, the products all come to life and happily sing the title song. An Eskimo falls for a cookie and has to come to the rescue when a swarm of flies invades.

metas.name: Why Do I Dream Those Dreams
metas.description: Rip van Winkle gets the musical cartoon treatment...

metas.name: The Girl at the Ironing Board
metas.description: An early Merrie Melodies featuring the title song.

metas.name: The Miller's Daughter
metas.description: Ceramic figurines come to life after one of them is knocked over and broken by the household cat.

metas.name: Shake Your Powder Puff
metas.description: In this one, we're witness to a sort of vaudeville show with an all-animal cast, including a myopic turtle and a pig very proud of his ability to play the flute. There's a troupe of dancing "girls" who sing about "shaking your powder puff," and a dog (or wolf, or fox or something) keeps getting thro

metas.name: Those Beautiful Dames
metas.description: Toys in a shop window come to life and visit a poverty-stricken little girl as she sleeps. She awakens to find that her shack has been refurbished and that the toys are about to throw her a party.

metas.name: Pop Goes Your Heart
metas.description: A robin sings, and the vegetation turns spring-like, followed by some more action by birds and bees...

metas.name: Mr. and Mrs. Is the Name
metas.description: A merman boy and mermaid girl play, explore a sunken ship, and deal with a giant octopus.

metas.name: Country Boy
metas.description: Mother rabbit sends her charges off to school. Peter needs a bit more attention; he's hiding with the chickens, using a feather duster to stand in for a tail. On his way to school, Peter starts to sneak into a farmer's field, but is caught by three schoolmates. They threaten to tell the teacher, and

metas.name: I Haven't Got a Hat
metas.description: It's recital day at the schoolhouse. First up: Porky, who recites The Midnight Ride of Paul Revere. A nervous kitten recites Mary Had a Little Lamb. The puppies Ham and Ex sing the title song. Oliver Owl plays the piano; Beans the cat puts a cat and dog inside, and they play a tune as well.

metas.name: Along Flirtation Walk
metas.description: Chickens from Plymouth Rock College and the Rhode Island Reds prepare for the big game.

metas.name: My Green Fedora
metas.description: A rabbit is told by his mother to watch out for his baby brother Elmer while she's out of the house, but a wolf has other plans for Elmer after he hears the older brother sing "My Green Fedora."

metas.name: Into Your Dance
metas.description: The showboat comes to town, piloted by Captain Benny. A quartet sings "Go Into Your Dance" in honor of its originator, Al Jolson. They introduce the conductor, who is a pig caricature of orchestra leader Paul Whiteman. One of the musicians plugs the pig's tail into a light socket so he conducts at s

metas.name: Country Mouse
metas.description: A strong mouse says that he will become the heavyweight champion of the world. But his grandma (who is just as strong) doesn't want him to fight...

metas.name: The Merry Old Soul
metas.description: Old King Cole marries the Woman in the Shoe. As soon as they get home, the babies show up from every drawer and closet, much to the king's chagrin.

metas.name: The Lady in Red
metas.description: At a Spanish restaurant, the owner is at the bullfights and the restaurant is closed. The roaches come out to eat, drink and be merry. At a roach night club, a comely little female roach, dressed in red, flamenco dances for an appreciative crowd. A pet parrot escapes his cage and finds the night clu

metas.name: Little Dutch Plate
metas.description: A cheery tune in a Dutch kitchen; the girl on the plate and the salt shaker boy are in love. They dance....

metas.name: Billboard Frolics
metas.description: Billboards come to life. Eddie Camphor and his "wioleen" player Rub-Him-Off do a song and dance to "Merrily We Roll Along" with new lyrics...

metas.name: Flowers for Madame
metas.description: A tour of the garden, where every flower dances or plays a tune, especially today, since it's the flower pageant. Fire strikes as a badly placed magnifying glass ignites a match. The flowers do what they can to fight it, but the fire manages to get through the sprinkler.

metas.name: I Wanna Play House
metas.description: Two bear cubs, one black, one brown, frolic near their sleeping father.

metas.name: The Cat Came Back
metas.description: Mama cat is teaching her kittens to catch mice. Meanwhile, across the basement, mama mouse is teaching her little ones how to avoid cats.

metas.name: I'm a Big Shot Now
metas.description: A tough bird proclaims his hatred of cops, with serious consequences.

metas.name: Let It Be Me
metas.description: A radio crooner spirits a girl away to the big city only to drop her like a hot potato.

metas.name: Bingo Crosbyana
metas.description: Bugs take over a kitchen, prompting a Bing Crosby-esque croon.

metas.name: When I Yoo Hoo
metas.description: It's the Weavers vs. the Mathews in Hickory Holler. The Weavers are singing (the title song), the Mathews are sleeping...

metas.name: Sunday Go to Meetin' Time
metas.description: A Black man sneaks out of church and tries to steal a chicken, but gets a taste of Hell when he's accidentally knocked unconscious. One of the "Censored 11" banned from TV syndication by United Artists in 1968 for racist stereotyping.

metas.name: At Your Service Madame
metas.description: Mrs. Hamhock finds herself the object of unwanted attention following an article in the paper about...

metas.name: Toy Town Hall
metas.description: A child would rather listen to the radio than go to bed, but mother insists. He sleeps, but at midnight, his toys come alive and put on a show for him (much of it recycled, though often with different backgrounds, from earlier cartoons).

metas.name: Boulevardier from the Bronx
metas.description: A baseball team full of anthropomorphic animals play on.

metas.name: The CooCoo Nut Grove
metas.description: A visit to a Hollywood nightclub, featuring caricatures of, among others, Walter Winchell, Hugh Herbert, W.C. Fields, Katharine Hepburn, Ned Sparks, Johnny Weissmuller, Lupe Velez, John Barrymore, Harpo Marx, George Arliss, Mae West, Stan Laurel, Oliver Hardy, Clark Gable, Edna May Oliver, Gary Coop

metas.name: He Was Her Man
metas.description: A Depression-era female mouse has to sell apples in the miserable cold, and then bring them home to her abusive husband. But when he abandons her and takes up with another woman, she does what any woman has the right to do.

metas.name: Pigs Is Pigs
metas.description: A hungry little pig eats a couple of pies off the windowsill. When it's time for dinner, he ties together the spaghetti of all the other little pigs and eats it all. That night, he has a nightmare where he is force-fed by a mad scientist.

metas.name: The Fella with a Fiddle
metas.description: A mouse fakes blindness and plays his fiddle; he returns home, where it becomes apparent he's rich. The tax collector arrives, and he pulls various levers and presses buttons to make his home look like a shack. The tax collector can't catch him. A cat sees this and tries baiting a trap with a gold c

metas.name: She Was an Acrobat's Daughter
metas.description: An evening at the local movie theater, including a sing-along led by Maestro Stickoutski at the Mighty Fertilizer organ, a Goofy-Tone newsreel, and the feature, Petrified Florist, featuring caricatures of Bette Davis and Leslie Howard.

metas.name: Clean Pastures
metas.description: The Lord sees that the stock value of "Pair-o-dice" is dropping on the exchange so he dispatches a slow-witted and slow-talking angel to sinful Harlem to recruit new customers. When this fails, God finds success sending a group of musical angels with a little more swing in their style, so much so th

metas.name: Streamlined Greta Green
metas.description: In a world wherein cars act like humans, Junior wants to be a taxi, but his mother wants him to grow up to be a nice touring car like his father. Mom doesn't know that Junior sometimes skips school and ventures into the city to ride in traffic, drink hi-test gas, and race trains.

metas.name: Sweet Sioux
metas.description: Gags in a Native American village lead up to the tribe's attack on a covered wagon to the tune of "The Merry-Go-Round Broke Down," the first use of the song in a Warner Bros. cartoon.

metas.name: Plenty of Money and You
metas.description: A hen's chicks hatch, but one of them is actually an ostrich. She treats it as her own, but the ostrich keeps getting into trouble.

metas.name: Dog Daze
metas.description: A series of gags at a dog show, including a stage revue. A dog gets into a trunk of roller skates and crashes through the stage show.

metas.name: The Lyin' Mouse
metas.description: A mouse is trying to free himself from a trap when a cat arrives. The mouse, desperate, asks if the cat has heard the story of the lion and the mouse.

metas.name: September in the Rain
metas.description: The rain is outdoors; the action is indoors, in a grocery store, where the characters on product labels come to life.

metas.name: My Little Buckeroo
metas.description: In the border town of Boiled Beef, Texas, in 1872, a bandit who is wanted by authorities terrorizes the town - but a pig-headed deputy thinks he has a way to capture him.

metas.name: Jungle Jitters
metas.description: Starts out with a tribe of African cannibals imitating Native Americans. After this, they do the new Warner Bros. Looney Tunes theme "The Merry-Go-Round Broke Down." Then a sloppy stuttering salesman knocks on their doors, and they bring him in and put him in a pot of boiling water. The queen of the

metas.name: A Star Is Hatched
metas.description: Emily the chicken lives in Hickville but dreams of Hollywood. Her chance comes when director J. Megga-Phone happens to drive past and gives her his card.

metas.name: Confederate Honey
metas.description: Nett Cutler (Elmer Fudd) romances Crimson O'Hairoil in this send-up of Gone With the Wind (1939).

metas.name: The Hardship of Miles Standish
metas.description: In this version of "The Courtship of Miles Standish", Elmer Fudd is messanger John Alden, sent to give Miles' love letter to Priscilla. While delivering the message, however, her house is attacked by Indians, and John is the only one who can save her.

metas.name: You Ought to Be in Pictures
metas.description: Daffy Duck convinces Porky Pig to quit the cartoon biz and try his luck in the features. Porky's adventures begin when he tries to enter the movie studio.

metas.name: Porky's Baseball Broadcast
metas.description: Porky Pig provides play-by-play radio-broadcast commentary during a World Series baseball game.

metas.name: Little Blabbermouse
metas.description: A mouse, imitating W.C. Fields, leads a nighttime tour of a closed drugstore for other mice, that include a very inquisitive little boy.

metas.name: Malibu Beach Party
metas.description: Jack Bunny (a spoof of Jack Benny) invites Hollywood celebrities to his Malibu house for a party.

metas.name: Calling Dr. Porky
metas.description: A dog thinks he is being chased by small pink elephants, and goes to the hospital. While Porky is working on medication, the pink elephants find him and cause havoc. Porky finally gives him some medication, that only works temporarily, but then sees them again. He rushes back in and is once again il

metas.name: Porky's Hired Hand
metas.description: Porky hires on Gregory Grunt to watch over his chicken coop to stop the fox from raiding it. He falls asleep, and the fox fills his bag. But Grunt wakes up and confronts the fox who then talks him into becoming his partner. As the fox is leaving, he locks himself into the incubator room by mistake.

metas.name: Shop Look & Listen
metas.description: J.T. Gimlet's department store is closed, and the mice are going on a tour, led by the same W.C. Fields mouse as in Little Blabbermouse. First, the shoe department, where we see mules, both red and green, who pop out of the box and bray at us. Next, the artworks: Whistler's Mother proves to be a goo

metas.name: The Fighting 69½th
metas.description: Battalions of red and black ants go to war over an unattended picnic blanket full of food.

metas.name: The Cat's Tale
metas.description: The mouse, tired of being chased by the cat, convinces him there's no reason for it, and that the cat should talk to the dog and convince him too. The talks are not successful...

metas.name: Porky's Bear Facts
metas.description: Porky Pig works hard on his farm all year. On a neighboring farm, a bear lazes around and allows his animals to be idle. The winter comes, and he has nothing to eat.

metas.name: The Trial of Mr. Wolf
metas.description: The Big Bad Wolf is on trial for crimes committed against Little Red Riding Hood and her grandmother. When given a chance to speak in his defense, Mr. Wolf explains the supposed real story: He is the victim.

metas.name: Hiawatha's Rabbit Hunt
metas.description: Bugs Bunny is hunted by Hiawatha, a stereotyped Native American who fills roughly the same role as Elmer Fudd in other Bugs Bunny cartoons of this era.

metas.name: The Wacky Worm
metas.description: A worm is pursued by a crow.

metas.name: Sport Chumpions
metas.description: An outlet highlights on sports champions and sporting events, "bringing you lowlights in the world of sports"

metas.name: Notes to You
metas.description: Without success, Porky Pig tries to silence an alley cat who has been disturbing his slumber by constantly singing loudly.

metas.name: Rookie Revue
metas.description: Random gags around military life, set on an army base. A bugler uses a jukebox to play reveille. In formation, one private has a great deal of trouble remembering what comes after "3"; after he gets it, he decides not to go for the $32 question. In the mess hall, the machine gunners machine gun thei

metas.name: Rhapsody in Rivets
metas.description: A construction foreman conducts his workers like a symphony orchestra as they build a skyscraper to Franz Liszt's "Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2."

metas.name: Hop, Skip and a Chump
metas.description: A grasshopper toys with two crows trying to catch him.

metas.name: Porky's Pastry Pirates
metas.description: Porky Pig owns a bakery. Enter a bee and a fly.

metas.name: The Wabbit Who Came to Supper
metas.description: Bugs Bunny exploits the situation when an uncle leaves Elmer Fudd three million dollars on the condition that he harm no animals, especially rabbits.

metas.name: Saps in Chaps
metas.description: Sagebrush site gags depicting wild west wackiness.

metas.name: Lights Fantastic
metas.description: A tour of the bright lights of New York City, where the various advertising signs come to life.

metas.name: Double Chaser
metas.description: A mouse, being chased by a cat, enlists the help of a sleeping bulldog. When the dog awakes, the mouse hides in a hen's nest, and the cat disguises himself as a hen - and even does a hen imitation when the chicks hatch. The mouse then keeps pointing out the cat's hiding places, but when he points to

metas.name: Foney Fables
metas.description: A series of fractured fairy tales vignettes.

metas.name: Fresh Hare
metas.description: Bugs Bunny is wanted "dead or alive" by the Mounted Police, led by Elmer Fudd. The "Fresh Hare" episode was banned from television for almost 30 years because it was considered too racey for the time.

metas.name: The Sheepish Wolf
metas.description: Sam Sheepdog and Ralph Wolf are both just trying to do what they have to do.

metas.name: The Hare-Brained Hypnotist
metas.description: Elmer Fudd goes after Bugs using hypnotism, only the plan backfires.

metas.name: Ding Dog Daddy
metas.description: A dumb mutt falls in love with the metal statue of a greyhound.

metas.name: Pigs in a Polka
metas.description: A tuxedo-clad wolf Master of Ceremonies announces the evening's program: the tale of the Big Bad Wolf and the Three Little Pigs, set to the music of Johannes Brahms's Hungarian Dances. Queue the fairy tale.

metas.name: Greetings Bait
metas.description: A worm reminiscent of Jerry Colonna is lowered into the water and uses various guises to lure fish. He also tangles with a crab.

metas.name: Yankee Doodle Daffy
metas.description: Daffy is an agent representing Sleepy Lagoon, trying to sell him to talent scout Porky. Daffy spends a great deal of time and energy explaining and demonstrating what the kid can do, while the kid sits on a couch licking a giant sucker.

metas.name: Jack-Wabbit and the Beanstalk
metas.description: Bugs Bunny encounters the legendary giant.

metas.name: Fifth Column Mouse
metas.description: In an allegory for World War II, one mouse's attempt to appease the cat of the house in exchange for a regular supply of cheese puts all the mice in danger.

metas.name: Hiss and Make Up
metas.description: An old woman has a cat, a dog, and a canary. The cat and dog fight even worse than normally. Fed up, she tells them both off, then threatens to throw them both out if there's any more trouble.

metas.name: Daffy - The Commando
metas.description: Commando Daffy Duck goes behind enemy lines and causes havoc for a Nazi German officer and his troops.

metas.name: Little Red Riding Rabbit
metas.description: Bugs, the Wolf and bobby-soxer Red chase each other around while Grandma is off working at Lockheed aircraft.

metas.name: Meatless Flyday
metas.description: A hungry spider is trying to catch a fly for dinner. Both pull pranks on each other until the fly is finally caught.

metas.name: Bugs Bunny Nips the Nips
metas.description: Bugs fights stereotyped Japanese during World War II.

metas.name: Duck Soup to Nuts
metas.description: Porky Pig is out hunting duck, but Daffy shows him that he is no ordinary duck.

metas.name: Slightly Daffy
metas.description: General Daffy, in a Napoleon hat, commands a fort. Porky sleeps too soundly, so Daffy needs to roust him, but when the Indians attack, he's the only one awake to see them.

metas.name: Hare Force
metas.description: Granny lets Bugs Bunny come in from the cold, but her dog Sylvester will have none of it.

metas.name: Goldilocks and the Jivin' Bears
metas.description: The stories of "Goldilocks" and "Little Red Riding Hood" collide with the world of jazz, resulting in three jiving bears and a jitterbugging Big Bad Wolf.  One of the “Censored 11” banned from TV syndication by United Artists in 1968 for racist stereotyping.

metas.name: Stage Door Cartoon
metas.description: That wascawwy wabbit is chased into a theatre by Elmer Fudd, and ends up having to perform to save himself, as well as convince Elmer to act himself. The vaudeville industry was never this wacky!

metas.name: Herr Meets Hare
metas.description: Bugs disguises himself as Hitler, Stalin and Brunhilde when he confronts Nazi Hermann Goering in the Black Forest.

metas.name: Life with Feathers
metas.description: A spurned love bird tries to get Sylvester to put him out of his misery.

metas.name: Hare Trigger
metas.description: Yosemite Sam is trying to rob the train that Bugs Bunny is riding on, and the two face off in several different ways.

metas.name: Ain't That Ducky
metas.description: Daffy Duck hears a duckling crying, arousing Daffy, so he asks the duckling why he is so sad. The duckling is short-tempered and cried, until the hunter succeeded in stealing the satchel reads a note finding out why the duckling is so sad.

metas.name: Peck Up Your Troubles
metas.description: Sylvester is determined to get a woodpecker that just moved in, high in a tree. He climbs, but the bird greases the tree; he starts to cut it down, but a mean dog stops him (this becomes a running gag). Several other attempts follow; at one point, he puts his paw into the bird's home, and the bird p

metas.name: Baseball Bugs
metas.description: Bugs Bunny single handedly takes on the “Gas-House Gorillas,” a baseball team of hulking, cigar-chomping bullies.

metas.name: Holiday for Shoestrings
metas.description: To the tune of The Nutcracker, a number of elves do all the work in a shoe shop.

metas.name: Hollywood Daffy
metas.description: Daffy sneaks onto the Warmer Brothers lot, eventually posing as a tour guide. Daffy spoofs a number of contemporary stars, and others appear as "themselves". He also has a number of run-ins with a studio cop.

metas.name: Of Thee I Sting
metas.description: A mosquito army trains for, then goes on, an attack mission.

metas.name: Racketeer Rabbit
metas.description: Hugo and Rocky (caricatures of Edward G. Robinson and Peter Lorre) make it home to their hideout only to find Bugs already settled down there for the night.

metas.name: Rhapsody Rabbit
metas.description: When Bugs Bunny attempts to perform Liszt's Second Hungarian Rhapsody, he is troubled by a mouse.

metas.name: The Gay Anties
metas.description: The 1890s; a picnic in the park. A man is pitching woo to his girl, while behind them a steady stream of ants is methodically devouring and carting off their food. Some other interludes include four ants eating Russian rye bread, then breaking for a Russian dance; a torch singer that sends everyone

metas.name: A Hare Grows in Manhattan
metas.description: Bugs Bunny relates his early life in the Manhattan tenements and spotlights his encounter with a gang of canine toughs.

metas.name: Tweetie Pie
metas.description: Thomas the cat finds Tweetie in the snow, warming himself by a cigar butt. Thomas's mistress rescues the little yellow bird before her cat can devour him, but Thomas doesn't give up.

metas.name: Rabbit Transit
metas.description: This time Bugs' race with Cecil Turtle features a rocket-powered tortoise shell.

metas.name: Along Came Daffy
metas.description: Snowbound in a remote cabin, two starving men begin visualizing each other as food. When salesman Daffy Duck calls at their door, it doesn't take long before the men set their minds on having Daffy as their dinner.

metas.name: Slick Hare
metas.description: Humphrey Bogart visits the Mocrumbo Restaurant. He orders fried rabbit and Elmer Fudd has twenty minutes to serve it.

metas.name: Back Alley Oproar
metas.description: Sylvester sings opera and popular tunes while standing on a back alley fence; Elmer, who wants to sleep, tries to thwart him.

metas.name: I Taw a Putty Tat
metas.description: Woman wonders why her little pet birds keep disappearing. Sylvester the cat knows, but other than burping feathers, he's not saying. But it looks like he's met his match when the woman orders another bird from the pet shop: a little yellow canary named "Tweety".

metas.name: Buccaneer Bunny
metas.description: Yosemite Sam as a pirate makes the mistake of trying to bury his treasure chest in Bugs' hole, and pays with the loss of his ship.

metas.name: Bugs Bunny Rides Again
metas.description: In the Western town of Rising Gorge, Bugs faces off against Yosemite Sam, "the roughest, toughest, he-man stuffest hombre who's ever crossed the Rio Grande."

metas.name: Hare Splitter
metas.description: When Bugs arrives for his date with Daisy Lou and finds her out shopping, he puts on her clothes to fool his rival Casbah.

metas.name: Kit for Cat
metas.description: Elmer Fudd takes in Sylvester Cat and an orange kitten during a cold winter night. He'd like to adopt both, but can only keep one. He decides to go to bed and make up his mind in the morning. Sylvester and the kitten both want to be the one who is adopted, so each tries framing the other for noisy m

metas.name: Wise Quackers
metas.description: Daffy Duck falls from the sky onto Elmer Fudd's farm. Rather than be shot, he begs Elmer to accept him as a personal slave. After torturing Elmer with his type of kindness, slave Daffy puts a whip in Elmer's hands, then instantly dresses like Abraham Lincoln to scold Elmer for "whipping slaves".

metas.name: Hare Do
metas.description: Elmer Fudd chases Bugs Bunny all the way from the woods to a local movie theater, where cinema-related hijinks ensue.

metas.name: High Diving Hare
metas.description: Yosemite Sam tries to force Bugs Bunny to do a high-diving act when the regular act cancels.

metas.name: Curtain Razor
metas.description: Porky, a talent scout for "Goode and Korney Talent Agency," auditions various acts. A final gag has a wolf performing this "stupendous act" where he wears a devil hat, cape and the like, drinks nitroglycerin, gasoline and other explosive stuff, then swallows a match. KABOOM! Porky thinks that the ac

metas.name: Mouse Mazurka
metas.description: In the Slobovian mountains, Sylvester Cat and a mouse move to the tune of East European folk music as this chase cartoon is propelled to an explosive climax.

metas.name: Knights Must Fall
metas.description: Bugs must joust with Sir Pantsalot of Drop Seat Manor when he tosses a partially eaten carrot into a suit of armor.

metas.name: Bad Ol' Putty Tat
metas.description: Sylvester Cat starts to saw down Tweety Bird's house. Tweety flees into a badminton court, where he becomes the birdie in the game. Sylvester disguises himself as a player, and Tweety drops a TNT stick into Sylvester's mouth.

metas.name: Dough for the Do-Do
metas.description: Porky Pig has an adventure in Wackyland while searching for the last Do-Do bird.

metas.name: Each Dawn I Crow
metas.description: Chided by a narrator, John Rooster thinks Elmer Fudd is going to slaughter him with an axe for Sunday dinner and is willing to do anything to prevent his hour of doom.

metas.name: Which Is Witch
metas.description: Dr. I.C. Spots is an African witch doctor about to prepare a potion which needs as one of its ingredient a rabbit.

metas.name: Home, Tweet Home
metas.description: Tweety Bird is washing in a bird bath in a city park when Sylvester Cat interrupts him. Sylvester chases Tweety, and Tweety takes refuge near a feisty nanny and her toddler. Sylvester dresses as the toddler to try to grab Tweety but is stopped and spanked. Tweety flies to a building ledge, and Sylve

metas.name: Mutiny on the Bunny
metas.description: Shanghai Sam needs a new crew for his ship. Bugs signs on but rebels at the captain's cruelty.

metas.name: The Lion's Busy
metas.description: In an African jungle, hungry Beaky Buzzard can't wait until Leo the Lion is decently deceased before trying to devour him. Leo takes a rocket to the Moon to try to escape Beaky, but finds Beaky already there waiting for him.

metas.name: Big House Bunny
metas.description: While attempting to evade a group of hunters, Bugs Bunny jumps into a rabbit hole and inadvertently tunnels into Sing Song prison, where the malevolent prison guard, Sam Schultz, assumes he's an inmate.

metas.name: His Bitter Half
metas.description: Daffy Duck marries for money, but the bossy wife and her raucous, trouble-making little son soon have him wanting out.

metas.name: All a Bir-r-r-d
metas.description: Tweety Bird is on a train with Sylvester.

metas.name: Golden Yeggs
metas.description: On Porky Pig's farm, a goose lays a golden egg and says that Daffy Duck laid it. Daffy, now the most sought-after duck in the world, is quite willing to take the credit and resultant fame- until Rocky the gangster kidnaps Daffy and orders him at gunpoint to lay more.

metas.name: Bunker Hill Bunny
metas.description: Sam Von Schamm The Hessian and Bugs Bunny fight it out in the little known American Revolutionary War Battle of Bagel Heights.

metas.name: Canary Row
metas.description: Sylvester Cat spots Tweety Bird in a San Francisco apartment and tries to gain access but cannot make it past Granny or the cat-hating desk clerk.

metas.name: Stooge for a Mouse
metas.description: A crafty mouse decides to remove his one obstacle to obtaining a block of cheese - Sylvester Cat - by stirring up trouble between Sylvester and Mike the Bulldog, two buddies turned to enemies by the mouse's clever set-ups implicating Sylvester in attacks on Mike.

metas.name: Canned Feud
metas.description: Sylvester Cat finds that his people have gone on vacation and left him alone in a locked house with a large stash of canned food in a cupboard. Sylvester needs a can opener, or he'll starve. And a pesky mouse has the only can opener in the house and torments Sylvester into trying more and more despe

metas.name: Rabbit Every Monday
metas.description: Yosemite Sam traps Bugs Bunny and tries to cook him -- until he sees that Bugs is having a party and wants to join in the fun.

metas.name: Putty Tat Trouble
metas.description: Tweety Bird is shoveling out his nest atop a city pole after a snowstorm and is spotted by Sylvester Cat and a one-eyed orange tabby, who fight over Tweety. Tweety runs into a cellar where he befriends a wooden dunking bird. The two cats then chase Tweety into a park and onto a sheet of ice covering

metas.name: A Bone for a Bone
metas.description: Two polite gophers are in their underground home, playing gin, when a dog buries his bone right on top of them. They try to negotiate with the dog so that he will bury the bone elsewhere. But the dog refuses to be cooperative.

metas.name: The Fair Haired Hare
metas.description: Yosemite Sam and Bugs battle it out over property rights above Bugs' rabbit hole.

metas.name: Room and Bird
metas.description: Tweety and Sylvester are Granny's pets in the Spinsters Arms Hotel, where pets aren't allowed.

metas.name: Tweety's S.O.S.
metas.description: Sylvester Cat stows away aboard a seagoing passenger liner to try and catch Tweety Bird, who is guarded by his mistress, Granny. Sylvester becomes seasick and runs to the sickbay for a remedy. Tweety mixes nitro into the medicine before Sylvester drinks it. When Granny hits Sylvester with her broom,

metas.name: Ballot Box Bunny
metas.description: When Yosemite Sam campaigns on a platform including rabbit genocide, Bugs Bunny runs against him.

metas.name: Tweet Tweet Tweety
metas.description: Sylvester Cat leaves a trailer in a National Forest Camping Ground to go bird hunting and discovers an egg in a nest. Sylvester decides to sit on the egg to hatch it, and when it hatches, out crawls Tweety Bird! Sylvester chases Tweety into a geyser and down a river in a boat toward a waterfall.

metas.name: Gift Wrapped
metas.description: It's Christmas Day in the home of Granny, and her pet cat Sylvester delights at chasing her new Tweety Bird and takes fright at the bulldog unwrapped from under the tree.

metas.name: Foxy by Proxy
metas.description: Bugs is provoked by a pack of foxhounds and their hunters stampeding over his hole, so he gets out his Halloween costume from last year (a fox suit) and sets out to lead the dogs on a merry chase. The stupidest of the dogs, whose objective is to cut a fox's tail off, becomes his main victim; Bugs tr

metas.name: 14 Carrot Rabbit
metas.description: Yosemite Sam (as Chilikoot Sam) tries unsuccessfully to steal gold from Bugs Bunny during the Yukon gold rush.

metas.name: Little Red Rodent Hood
metas.description: An elderly mouse tells the bedtime story of Little Red Riding Hood to her grandson, who visualizes the tale in cat-and-mouse terms, with himself as Red and Sylvester as the Big Bad Wolf.

metas.name: Ain't She Tweet
metas.description: Sylvester Cat discovers Tweety Bird in a pet store window. Tweety is taken to be delivered by truck to a new owner - Granny. Sylvester chases the delivery truck to Granny's home, where Granny has a huge, fenced-in area for her army of bulldogs. Sylvester makes several unsuccessful attempts to pass t

metas.name: Cracked Quack
metas.description: Daffy Duck takes shelter from a blizzard by sneaking into a cozy home owned by Porky Pig. Daffy tries to secretly mooch off of Porky for an entire winter, but Porky's dog realizes that Daffy isn't the stuffed ornament he pretends to be and keeps trying to alert Porky to Daffy's ruse.

metas.name: A Bird in a Guilty Cage
metas.description: Sylvester Cat spots Tweety Bird in a display window of an after-hours department store and sneaks inside through a mail server chute. Tweety flees Sylvester by hiding in a hat pile and a doll house, evades the shots from a rifle Sylvester uses, and escapes in a vacuum tube. Tweety sends a dynamite s

metas.name: Tree for Two
metas.description: A rough and tough bulldog named Spike sets out with his admirer, a small dog named Chester, to rough up a cat. They encounter Sylvester and chase him into a junkyard, where a black panther that escaped from a zoo just happens to be hiding out. Every time Spike goes into the junkyard to thrash Sylves

metas.name: Hare Lift
metas.description: Bank robber Yosemite Sam forces Bugs to try to fly the largest airplane in the world.

metas.name: Snow Business
metas.description: Sylvester Cat and Tweety Bird are snowbound in a mountain cabin, and though Tweety has lots of bird seed, Sylvester will starve unless he can cook the unsuspecting Tweety. Meanwhile, a starving mouse thinks Sylvester is edible.

metas.name: A Mouse Divided
metas.description: A drunken stork delivers a baby mouse to the home of Mr. and Mrs. Sylvester Cat. Sylvester is about to eat the little rodent when it calls him Daddy. Touched, Sylvester adopts the mouse as his son - which, distressingly, attracts every hungry cat in the neighborhood to his door!

metas.name: Fowl Weather
metas.description: After Granny leaves a bulldog named Hector to guard Tweety while she's away from her farm, Sylvester manages to sneak in disguised as a scarecrow and soon gets more than he bargained for.

metas.name: Southern Fried Rabbit
metas.description: Bugs Bunny attempts to shake off Yosemite Sam (here, cast as a Civil War-era colonel), who is preventing him from crossing the Mason-Dixon Line.

metas.name: Ant Pasted
metas.description: Elmer Fudd, on a fourth of July picnic, throws some of his firecrackers into an ant colony, and the ants declare all-out war on him.

metas.name: Hare Trimmed
metas.description: Yosemite Sam hears that Granny has inherited fifty million dollars. Good guy Bugs tries to save Granny from Sam's clutches.

metas.name: Tom Tom Tomcat
metas.description: Tweety Bird is being taken by his mistress, Granny, on a trip across a prairie in a horse-drawn wagon when they are attacked by a tribe of Indian cats, all of whom are Sylvester or Sylvester variants.

metas.name: A Street Cat Named Sylvester
metas.description: The title of this cartoon is a misnomer, because it is in fact Tweety Bird who is the homeless one here, and Sylvester is Granny's pet. Tweety seeks shelter from a blizzard and taps on Granny's house door. Sylvester answers and grabs the canary. He tries to hide Tweety from Granny while evading the

metas.name: Catty Cornered
metas.description: Rocky the gangster kidnaps Tweety Bird for a million dollar ransom and holes up in an abandoned city building...

metas.name: Robot Rabbit
metas.description: Bugs Bunny faces off against Farmer Fudd's robot.

metas.name: Dog Pounded
metas.description: Sylvester Cat tries to catch Tweety Bird, who is up in a tree in the middle of the city dog pound.

metas.name: Captain Hareblower
metas.description: Bugs will not bend to the threats of the pirate Yosemite Sam.

metas.name: I Gopher You
metas.description: Two polite twin gophers are indignant at the swiping of all their vegetables by "vandals" in trucks. They follow the trucks to a food processing plant and become caught in the machinery when they try to retrieve their property.

metas.name: Bugs and Thugs
metas.description: When Bugs calls a cab, he doesn't know it's the getaway car for a couple of bankrobbers (however, he does know the capital of Nevada).

metas.name: Dr. Jerkyl's Hide
metas.description: Two street tough canines chase Sylvester Cat into the lab of Dr. Jerkyl, where he drinks the Mr. Hyde formula.

metas.name: Muzzle Tough
metas.description: Tweety Bird moves into a city brownstone with his mistress, Granny. A stray Sylvester Cat watches them move in and delights on seeing Tweety. Another of Granny's pets is a bulldog who complicates Sylvester's plan to sneak up close enough to make a grab for Tweety. Sylvester unsuccessfully tries all

metas.name: Satan's Waitin'
metas.description: Sylvester's carnivorous pursuit of Tweety Bird continues, winding up the cat's spirit in Hell, where he meets a satanic bulldog.

metas.name: Yankee Doodle Bugs
metas.description: Bugs lectures his nephew Clyde about early America, inserting himself into events wherever possible.

metas.name: Goo Goo Goliath
metas.description: A drunken stork delivers the baby of a giant to a normal-sized couple instead, and they try to raise him as well as they can.

metas.name: By Word of Mouse
metas.description: Hans, a mouse from Germany, comes to America to visit his cousin Willie, and learns about the wonders of the capitalist system.

metas.name: Pizzicato Pussycat
metas.description: Mr. and Mrs. Jones hear a piano being played in their living room. They automatically assume it is their cat who is making the music, when in fact, the talented one is a mouse whom the cat has forced into being his stooge to make him famous. The cat is showered with media attention and set to play a

metas.name: Pests for Guests
metas.description: Elmer Fudd buys a wooden chest of drawers not knowing that two polite twin gophers (known as The Goofy Gophers) have claimed the piece of furniture as their new home.

metas.name: Stork Naked
metas.description: A drunken stork comes to the home of Mr. and Mrs. Daffy Duck with a bundle of joy, but Daffy wants no part of the delivery and takes extreme measures to keep the stork away.

metas.name: Sahara Hare
metas.description: Riff-Raff (Yosemite) Sam, riding a camel that won't whoa, chases Bugs into a French Foreign-Legion post.

metas.name: Sandy Claws
metas.description: Tweety Bird goes to the beach with Granny, and Sylvester tries once again to catch him.

metas.name: Hare Brush
metas.description: The corporate board has Elmer committed to an asylum because he thinks he's a rabbit. At the sanitarium, Bugs agrees to trade places with Elmer.

metas.name: Tweety's Circus
metas.description: Sylvester Cat pays a visit to a closed-to-business circus and finds Tweety Bird in one of the cages. Tweety escapes and a mad chase ensues. Meanwhile, Sylvester must flee from an uncaged lion he angered earlier.

metas.name: Lumber Jerks
metas.description: Two polite gophers find that their home, a tree, has been cut down and taken away. They find it in a log pile about to be taken inside a processing factory. Following it into there, they become caught in the daunting machinery.

metas.name: This Is a Life?
metas.description: Parody of "This is Your Life," with Elmer Fudd as the host and Bugs Bunny as the guest of honor, much to the disgust of Daffy Duck. On several occassions, Granny has to whack Daffy over the head to get him to be quiet. Meanwhile, Bugs reminisces with Elmer and Yosemite Sam about their previous encou

metas.name: A Kiddies Kitty
metas.description: To escape a bulldog, Sylvester Cat allows himself to be adopted by a little girl. The little girl turns out to be rougher than the bulldog, though in her case it is entirely out of love.

metas.name: Hyde and Hare
metas.description: Bugs Bunny manages to get himself adopted by kindly Dr. Jekyll, but is surprised when his benefactor turns into the horrible Mr. Hyde after drinking a potion.

metas.name: Speedy Gonzales
metas.description: Speedy comes to the aid of a group of mice trying to get the cheese from a factory guarded by Sylvester.

metas.name: Red Riding Hoodwinked
metas.description: Red Riding Hood is on her way from the city to the country, to visit Granny. She's bringing Tweety Bird to Granny as a gift - which attracts Sylvester's attention. Along the way she also meets the Big Bad Wolf. Sylvester wants to eat Tweety. Big Bad wants to eat Red.

metas.name: Roman Legion-Hare
metas.description: The Coliseum, Rome, 54 A.D. Yosemite Sam, as Captain of the Guard, is ordered by Emperor Nero to find a victim to toss to the lions, or else he'll be the victim. Shortly thereafter Sam encounters Bugs Bunny and decides he will make a good victim.

metas.name: Heir-Conditioned
metas.description: Sylvester is a rich cat, courtesy of his deceased mistress, who has left him $3 million. His alley cat friends, hope to sponge off his good fortune, and Sylvester is eager to share with them. But Elmer Fudd, as Sylvester's new financial advisor, lectures him on investing his wealth in business and i

metas.name: Pappy's Puppy
metas.description: Butch, a mean bulldog, teaches his young son about the facts of life, including how to attack cats. The pup is at first frightened when he encounters Sylvester, but the youngster (remembering his father's lesson) soon becomes a thorn in the pussycat's side.

metas.name: Tweet and Sour
metas.description: Sylvester Cat tries to catch Tweety Bird in Granny's farm house, but Granny catches Sylvester and warns him if anything ever happens to Tweety, she will have Sylvester turned into violin strings. A one-eyed orange tabby makes off with Tweety, and Sylvester must rescue the canary to avoid being sent

metas.name: Rabbitson Crusoe
metas.description: Crusoe, played by Yosemite Sam, has been living off coconuts for 20 years when Bugs washes up on his island.

metas.name: Tree Cornered Tweety
metas.description: Sylvester Cat chases Tweety Bird while Tweety narrates. The chase takes them out of the city to the country, straight into a mine field, down a ski slope, and to the middle of a wooden bridge, where Sylvster stupidly saws a hole, with himself in its center.

metas.name: Napoleon Bunny-Part
metas.description: Bugs takes a wrong turn off the Hollywood freeway and tunnels into the headquarters of Napoleon Bonaparte.

metas.name: Tugboat Granny
metas.description: Tweety Bird and Granny are at the controls of a tugboat that Sylvester tries unsuccessfully to board.

metas.name: A Star Is Bored
metas.description: Daffy Duck is hired to be the stunt double in any film which the Warner Brothers studio considers too dangerous for its star Bug Bunny.

metas.name: Yankee Dood It
metas.description: Elmer Fudd is the progressive King of industrial Elves. He visits an outmoded shoemaker's shop to extol the virtues of mass production capitalism to the shoemaker, whose pet cat, Sylvester, uses the magic word, "Jehosophat" to turn Fudd's elf helper into a mouse and chases him around the shoemaker's

metas.name: Two Crows from Tacos
metas.description: Two none-too-bright Mexicali crows chase a grasshopper who outwits them at every turn.

metas.name: Three Little Bops
metas.description: Three Little Pigs are hip travelling entertainers, moving from straw to wood to brick nightclubs, playing swinging tunes for high-class "with it" crowds, but uncool Big Bad Wolf keeps intruding on their act with with his "corny horn" and uses it to blow their nightclubs down when they throw him out.

metas.name: Tweet Zoo
metas.description: Sylvester Cat joins a tour group through the City Zoo and finds Tweety Bird among the exhibits. Sylvester chases Tweety and ends up in a bear's den.

metas.name: Tweety and the Beanstalk
metas.description: Jack's mother throws Jack's magic beans outside under Sylvester Cat's sleeping box, and the cat is whisked to the world above, where he finds a huge Tweety Bird in the castle of the legendary Giant.

metas.name: Piker's Peak
metas.description: In the Alps Bugs and Yosemite Sam vie for 50,000 Cronkites, the prize for the who "climbs the Schmatterhorn."

metas.name: Birds Anonymous
metas.description: In this spoof of Alcoholics Anonymous, pussycats are cast as bird-eating addicts and go through the 12-step process to deal with their addiction. Sylvester, who could never quite get the best of the object of his desire, Tweety Bird, joins and resolves to quit chasing and eating the canary.

metas.name: Bugsy and Mugsy
metas.description: Bugs Bunny finds that gangsters Rocky and Mugsy have chosen his new abode, a condemned building, as their hideout. Bugs manipulates them into attacking each other to prove that crime doesn't pay.

metas.name: Greedy for Tweety
metas.description: Sylvester Cat chases Tweety Bird into busy city streets as he himself is being chased by a bulldog. All three are in an accident and taken to an animal hospital, each with a broken leg.

metas.name: Show Biz Bugs
metas.description: Bugs and Daffy are vaudevillians competing for praise from the audience. They love Bugs no matter what; just the opposite for Daffy.

metas.name: Gonzales' Tamales
metas.description: Male Mexican mice are jealous of Speedy Gonzales for taking their girlfriends. So, they set Sylvester Cat after Speedy by issuing a challenge to Sylvester in Speedy's name.

metas.name: Hare-Less Wolf
metas.description: An absent-minded wolf sets out to catch Bugs for dinner but keeps forgetting what he was heading out to shoot in the first place.

metas.name: A Pizza Tweety-Pie
metas.description: Another wet and wild Sylvester Cat-Tweety Bird chase, this time in the flooded areas of Venice, Italy, where Granny has taken Tweety on vacation.

metas.name: A Waggily Tale
metas.description: A boy named Junior, who treats his dog, Elvis, cruelly, is scolded by his mother and sent to his room to have a nap.

metas.name: Knighty Knight Bugs
metas.description: King Arthur's kingdom and the knights of the Round Table are in the doldrums since the Dark Knight stole the Singing Sword and put it under the protection of a fire-breathing dragon. The king's jester, Bugs Bunny, says only a fool would try to steal it back, so the king orders him to try. The jester

metas.name: A Bird in a Bonnet
metas.description: The chase continues between Tweety Bird and that persistant puddy tat, Sylvester. Tweety hides in a millinery store (where Granny happens to be shopping) and hides on a hat.

metas.name: Trick or Tweet
metas.description: Sylvester Cat and a goony orange cat pretend not to let their rivalry over trying to catch Tweety Bird interfere with their friendship...

metas.name: Apes of Wrath
metas.description: The drunken stork loses the baby ape for Mr. and Mrs. Elvis Ape, so knocks out Bugs Bunny and delivers him instead.

metas.name: Mexicali Shmoes
metas.description: A pair of not-too-bright Mexican cats, one shorter-tempered than the other, decide to chase Speedy Gonzales, the fastest mouse in all Mexico.

metas.name: Tweet and Lovely
metas.description: Sylvester Cat's new hang-out is an inventor's lab, which is near Tweety Bird's house atop a pole.

metas.name: Wild and Woolly Hare
metas.description: Bugs Bunny and Yosemite Sam duel with trains in an Old West shootout.

metas.name: Here Today, Gone Tamale
metas.description: Sylvester Cat won't allow starving Mexican mice access to a cache of cheeses on a ship and prompts a challenge by Speedy Gonzales, the fastest mouse in Mexico. Speedy makes several raids on the ship's stores by outsmarting Sylvester again and again.

metas.name: Tweet Dreams
metas.description: Warners' "economy cartoon," repackaging footage from earlier Tweety and Sylvester chases with new footage. In this one, Sylvester tells a psychiatrist of his frustration at not being able to catch Tweety, his repeated failures illustrated through past cartoons featuring the canary and puddy tat.

metas.name: Horse Hare
metas.description: Yosemite Sam leads his Indians against Fort Lariat while Bugs is in charge.

metas.name: Goldimouse and the Three Cats
metas.description: Sylvester, his wife, and son go for a walk while their porridge cools, when Goldimouse wanders by to eat the porridge and sleep in their beds. Sylvester then tries to catch her for his "spoiled brat" of a son to eat.

metas.name: Person to Bunny
metas.description: In his Hollywood home Bugs is being interviewed by the Edward R. Murrow TV show "People to People" when Daffy and Elmer show up.

metas.name: Hyde and Go Tweet
metas.description: Sylvester alternates chasing the normal Tweety and fleeing a monster version of Tweety.

metas.name: Mouse and Garden
metas.description: Sylvester Cat and his orange feline friend, Sam, are rummaging through trash cans for food in the evening on a waterfront when they spot a mouse. They agree to share the little rodent for breakfast the next morning, while during the night each tries to snag the mouse for himself.

metas.name: From Hare to Heir
metas.description: Sam, the Duke of Yosemite, will inherit one million pounds if he can keep his temper in check. Thing is, he has to endure Bugs Bunny as his house guest.

metas.name: Trip for Tat
metas.description: Tweety Bird goes on a world tour with his mistress, Granny. And a hungry Sylvester Cat follows them everywhere they go (France, Japan, Switzerland, and Italy).

metas.name: Lighter Than Hare
metas.description: Outer space invader Yosemite Sam wants to capture typical earth creature Bugs Bunny.

metas.name: D' Fightin' Ones
metas.description: Sylvester Cat and a tough bulldog escape, chained together, from a transport vehicle headed for the city animal pound and make like convicts on the lam.

metas.name: The Rebel Without Claws
metas.description: The Confederate Army wants to get an important message through to General Lee, but all the carrier pigeons have been shot down. Tweety steps in.

metas.name: The Pied Piper of Guadalupe
metas.description: Sylvester the cat imitates the Pied Piper of Hamelin to lure a group of mice into a jug that he seals with a cork. But Speedy Gonzales won't be hypnotized by Sylvester's flute and gradually rescues his friends from Sylvester's clutches.

metas.name: Prince Violent
metas.description: Viking Yosemite Sam arrives to storm the castle. But Bugs takes charge of the defenses, and between Bugs' cleverness and Sam's stupidity, the castle is never seriously threatened, even when Sam enlists the help of an elephant.

metas.name: The Last Hungry Cat
metas.description: Sylvester Cat tumbles and falls dazed to the floor when making a grab for Tweety Bird. He comes to and thinks he has killed and swallowed the little canary and that he's wanted for murder.

metas.name: Crows' Feat
metas.description: Two Mexican crows, flying to Guadalajara on the wings of an airplane, spot a corn field on the ground below and dive into it...

metas.name: Mexican Boarders
metas.description: Speedy Gonzales' lethargic cousin, Slowpoke Rodriguez, comes to visit Speedy's hacienda, to the delight of Sylvester Cat, who is confident he will be able to catch Slowpoke for dinner.

metas.name: Honey's Money
metas.description: Yosemite Sam marries a wealthy widow for her money.

metas.name: The Jet Cage
metas.description: Tweety sits in his house, forlorn over the fact he can't fly outside like other birds because of his hungry feline predator, Sylvester.

metas.name: Shishkabugs
metas.description: A spoiled-rotten monarch orders royal chef Yosemite Sam to make "Hasenpfeffer", the basic ingredient of which is rabbit. When Bugs comes to the door asking to borrow some carrots, Sam decides to cook him!

metas.name: Devil's Feud Cake
metas.description: Another in a series of Warner's economy cartoons featuring clips from previous Bugs Bunny-Yosemite Sam cartoons. After Sam is killed in each pursuit, he meets with the devil, who goads him into continuing to chase the bunny.

metas.name: Mexican Cat Dance
metas.description: Mexican mice take over a bullfight ring after all the people have left, and they arrange their own entertainment, with Speedy Gonzales as a matador and Sylvester Cat substituting for a bull.

metas.name: Chili Weather
metas.description: Speedy Gonzales helps his fellow mice get food from the Guadalajara Food Processing plant, guarded by Sylvester the Cat.

metas.name: The Unmentionables
metas.description: In a spoof of TV's "Untouchables" Rocky and Mugsy chase "Elegant Ness" (Bugs) through the ACME cereal company.

metas.name: Nuts and Volts
metas.description: Sylvester Cat turns to automation in hopes it will help him catch the fastest mouse in Mexico, Speedy Gonzales. He builds a robot to chase Speedy around their house, but Speedy outsmarts Sylvester's new mechanical stooge, reducing it to a heap of scrap metal.

metas.name: Pancho's Hideaway
metas.description: A hot-tempered bandit, Pancho Vanilla, robs a Mexican bank and rushes to his hideout to count the loot. Speedy Gonzales, Mexico's fastest mouse, follows Pancho there, intending to return the money to the bank. He challenges Pancho to a duel and then speeds past him again and again, bringing every ce

metas.name: Road to Andalay
metas.description: Sylvester Cat uses a hunting bird, Malcolm Falcon, in another unsuccessful attempt to catch Speedy Gonzales, the fastest mouse in Mexico.

metas.name: It's Nice to Have a Mouse Around the House
metas.description: When Speedy Gonzales invades the home of Granny and rapidly drives her cat, Sylvester, to a nervous breakdown, Granny calls on Daffy Duck of the Jet Age Pest Control company to do the job of removing Gonzales from her home.

metas.name: Cats and Bruises
metas.description: Sylvester Cat intrudes on Speedy Gonzales' Cinco De Mayo celebration, starting a chase that ends in disaster.

metas.name: The Wild Chase
metas.description: Speedy Gonzales and the Road Runner are racing each other, with Sylvester Cat and Wile E. Coyote in hot pursuit.
